overview: India is a country in South Asia and the most populous country in the world. Its capital is New Delhi, and its biggest cities include Mumbai and Delhi. India has one of the world's oldest civilisations and is the birthplace of Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism. It became independent from the United Kingdom in 1947 and is the world's largest democracy. The central government uses Hindi and English, and the constitution recognises 22 languages.

geography.text: The Himalayas, the highest mountains on Earth, form India's northern border. South of them lie the wide plains of the Ganges and other great rivers, where many people live. The centre and south form the Deccan Plateau, edged by the Western and Eastern Ghats, and the peninsula is surrounded by the Arabian Sea, the Indian Ocean and the Bay of Bengal. The Thar Desert lies in the north-west, and the summer monsoon brings most of the year's rain.

history.text: The Indus Valley civilisation was one of the world's earliest. Over thousands of years India saw great empires, including the Maurya, the Gupta and the Mughals. Britain gradually took control from the 1700s. Mahatma Gandhi led a largely non-violent independence movement, and in 1947 British India was divided into India and Pakistan, a partition that caused huge violence and migration.

events.title: Indus cities
events.text: Great planned cities such as Mohenjo-daro flourish.

events.title: Emperor Ashoka
events.text: The Maurya emperor turns to Buddhism after a bloody war.

events.title: Indian Rebellion
events.text: A major uprising against British rule; Britain then takes direct control.

events.title: Independence and partition
events.text: India becomes independent and Pakistan is created.

events.title: Republic
events.text: India adopts its constitution and becomes a republic.

government.text: India is the world's largest democracy, a federal parliamentary republic of 28 states and 8 union territories. Voters elect the Lok Sabha, the lower house of parliament, and the leader with a majority becomes Prime Minister. The President is head of state. National elections involve nearly a billion voters and take several weeks.

economy.text: India has one of the largest and fastest-growing economies in the world. It is a global centre for IT services and software, a major producer of medicines and a growing manufacturer of phones and cars. Agriculture still employs a large share of people. India is the world's largest producer of milk.

culture.text: India has hundreds of languages, with Hindi and English used for central government and 22 languages recognised in the constitution. India makes more films than any other country, and Bollywood, based in Mumbai, is its most famous film industry. Yoga, chess and the decimal number system with zero all have roots in India.

items.title: Taj Mahal
items.text: A marble tomb built by Shah Jahan for his wife, finished around 1653.

items.title: Bollywood
items.text: The Hindi-language film industry, one of the largest in the world.

items.title: Diwali
items.text: The festival of lights, celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs and Jains.

sport.text: Cricket is India's great passion, and the Indian Premier League is one of the richest sports competitions in the world. India has won the men's Cricket World Cup twice, in 1983 and 2011, and the T20 World Cup in 2007 and 2024. Field hockey brought it eight Olympic golds, and Neeraj Chopra won javelin gold in 2021.

items.title: Field hockey
items.text: Eight Olympic gold medals, a record.

didYouKnow: India has the world's largest population, more than 1.4 billion people.
Chess, the decimal system and the number zero as a digit all developed in India.

keyPeople.name: Mahatma Gandhi
keyPeople.text: Led non-violent protest against British rule.

keyPeople.name: Kalpana Chawla
keyPeople.text: The first woman of Indian origin in space.
